Conjunction combines results into one result for a composite predicate: a
claim made of component claims, a decision over several evaluations, or
the outer contract of composed steps. It is defined here once, over the
core.

concepts.label: Conjunction of results

concepts.definition: Three separate conjunction inputs: applicable returned closed results with predicates and domain outcomes; planned assessments lacking an applicable closed result; and required coverage addressed by no planned assessment, computed as required obligations R minus admitted planned coverage C.

1. the closed results returned, each a core value with its predicate and
   domain outcome;
2. the planned assessments that have no closed result applicable to the
   composite: evaluations the composite requires that were not performed,
   or whose result is absent, stale, bound to another subject or basis, or
   incapable of establishing its claim;
3. the required coverage that no planned assessment addresses: for a
   required obligation set R and the coverage C that the planned
   assessments admit, the uncovered coverage R minus C.

conflict and indeterminacy are handled; which basis relations must agree,
results on different bases combining only under a declared coherent
composite basis (§2, Basis); which decision authority owns the
conjunction; how results that are not mandatory count; and whether any
result may veto or defer the decision.

algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special
case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on
the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted
conclusions, not a favourable selected run.

concepts.definition: Assertion provenance records the owning obligation, interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies of an expected result or acceptance predicate. Execution provenance records actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment, inputs, observations and result. grounding.quote:
An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the
owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared
dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution
provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,
inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they
support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected
answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned
assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and
evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a
third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).

assertions within their stated scope.

grounding.quote:

discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed
facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover
the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use
of evidence. A candidate selection is:
S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.

concepts.label: Ambiguity governance locators

conditions: An evaluation was performed.

grounding.quote:
This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Every performed evaluation returns exactly one core value directly or via a refinement. Constraints, judgments, frame evaluations, stops, work steps and effects use this one core or mapped refinements; a combination cannot hide or coerce a required failure, undecided question, unperformed evaluation or uncertain effect into success.

grounding.quote:
Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Record core value, evaluated predicate and original domain outcome; its definer retains domain meaning, and consumers needing that distinction read the domain outcome. Only satisfied establishes the predicate; falsified establishes failure and names its counterexample. Indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis establish neither truth nor failure and name respectively deciding evidence, missing relation/capability with owner where supplied, or basis repair. Satisfied stands above each other value by predicate support; the other four have no intrinsic ordering.

No mapping or refinement raises standing: failed/falsified never becomes successful/satisfied; undecidable never becomes satisfied; non-performance has no closed result and maps to no core value, including indeterminate; unknown effect completion never becomes no effect or completed.

conditions: An evaluation is required or planned but was not performed, or its result is missing.

grounding.quote:
Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.

constraints.statement: An actor cannot report an evaluation it did not perform. Non-performance has no closed result. Failed, indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope and invalid-basis outcomes follow their declared algebra rather than becoming satisfied. Missing results enter every relevant conjunction as planned-assessment gaps when planned, or uncovered coverage when no assessment was planned.
constraints.uncertainty: The source does not give a universal core mapping for every domain use of out-of-scope.

grounding.quote:
No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`.

constraints.statement: Refinements add no core value and keep indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis pressure explicit. If cause changes the mapped core value, encode cause in separate refined values, each mapping once. Every child names its parent and cause and keeps the parent's core value; a different core value requires a different parent declared only by the parent owner. No child acquires satisfied from a nonsatisfied parent. Mappings are stated where outcomes are defined; ACTIVATION §3 owns admission, activation and step refinements.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced ACTIVATION mappings are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step

constraints.statement: Producing a candidate establishes availability only, never fitness or acceptance. Assessment does not dispose at a boundary owned elsewhere. Acceptance belongs to its decision owner and boundary; no successful step, passing matrix, produced pack or decision(holds) alone supplies acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The exact acceptance boundary and authority are delegated to unavailable EVALUATION §5.

conditions: Classification depends on the activated frame's declarations and the evaluation actually available.
exceptions: Undeclared dependency and undecidable admissible evidence can coexist; out_of_frame and indeterminate each then have a lawful ground, and neither is excluded.

grounding.quote:
A term the claim depends on and the frame
  leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
  alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
  #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
  irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
- `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
  claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
  its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).

constraints.statement: A required relation or capability missing from the activated frame grounds out_of_frame regardless of what was exercised; name the missing item, its owner where supplied and reconfiguration pressure. A depended-on undefined term is such a material relation. Inability of available admissible evidence to decide grounds indeterminate and requires naming deciding evidence. Where both grounds hold, identify the returned value and its ground rather than imposing an unstated precedence.

conditions: A declared capability required by an evaluation was not exercised.
exceptions: A sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment can exist without the unexercised capability.

grounding.quote:
In either case
  the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
  it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
  failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
  The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
  result.

constraints.statement: Non-exercise of a declared capability has no core value of its own. Return an evidence-backed result if a sufficient evaluation or applicable judgment exists without it: a counterexample already found can falsify A and B by falsifying A, and agreement cannot discard it. Otherwise the evaluation was not performed and has no result; construction availability carries incomplete and work state retains the unexercised capability as residual. In either case the unexercised part remains a planned-assessment gap, with known failure surviving beside it. A step stop value never becomes its evaluation result.
constraints.uncertainty: The stop and work-state contracts are referenced, not fully supplied.

conditions: The corresponding imported concept, composition, transformation, reference, variation, sharing or categorical claim is used.

grounding.quote: for an evaluation that depends on a concept imported from another member, a missing source meaning, adoption or authority binding is a relation the frame does not declare, and a changed member or basis whose applicability is not re-established cannot support the evaluation
a categorical claim is established only with its demonstration, and without it is a hypothesis

constraints.statement: Missing imported source meaning, adoption or authority binding grounds out_of_frame; changed member/basis without re-established applicability cannot support evaluation. Composed steps require typed compatible preconditions, effects, results and authority, preserve both steps' produced facts and remain distinct from categorical joins; jointly used frames can instead contribute closed results to one conjunction. Every transformation records preserved, introduced and removed content, external witnesses and residuals; no fact is lost unrecorded. A reference substitutes for a body only if it supports the same consuming decision; otherwise shortfall remains residual, never success, and carrier/budget limits trim no required member. Lawful variation requires a declared relation; preference, probabilistic choice and human presence provide none. Repeated computation can propose shared machinery but decides no identity or authority; each instance retains responsibility and binding. Categorical claims require demonstrations, otherwise remaining hypotheses.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed composition licensing, conservation fields and categorical demonstration requirements refer to unsupplied owners.

conditions: Either gap input is nonempty.

grounding.quote:
Gaps. A conjunction with any item in the second or third input is never
`satisfied`. Its record names which kind of gap it has, not performed,
uncovered or both, and each item. An uncovered obligation is never
reported as satisfied or as an omitted planned assessment; a planned
assessment without a closed result is never reported as uncovered or as an
`indeterminate` component.

constraints.statement: A conjunction with either gap kind is never satisfied and records every item and whether it is not performed, uncovered or both. Uncovered obligations are neither satisfied nor omitted planned assessments. Planned assessments without closed results are neither uncovered nor indeterminate components.

conditions: A held result or an evaluation basis is stale, superseded, advanced, ambiguous, mismatched or bound to another subject/basis.

grounding.quote:
- an evaluation performed on a subject or basis that is stale, advanced,
  ambiguous or mismatched against the one it must bind returns
  `invalid_basis` for its own predicate, or is reactivated on the current
  basis; [RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)
  states this law over frames, and a conjunction that receives that
  `invalid_basis` holds it as a returned result;
- a component whose only held result is stale has no closed result
  applicable to the composite: on the basis the composite requires, its
  evaluation was not performed. It is a planned assessment without a
  closed result, in the second input, and a gap. Its stale value is
  neither counted as a returned result nor relabelled `invalid_basis` for
  the composite, and it stays in the record with its own basis;

constraints.statement: An evaluation actually performed on an unsuitable basis returns invalid_basis for its own predicate or is reactivated on the current basis; a received invalid_basis is a returned result. A component held only on a stale basis instead lacks an applicable result on the composite-required basis: it is a planned-assessment gap. Retain its stale result and original basis, but neither count nor relabel it invalid_basis for the composite; stale satisfied contributes nothing. Basis disagreement concerns returned results individually bound to their required bases that fail the declared agreement/coherence relations, not stale held values. One stale component is not answered both ways.

conditions: Conjunctions are joined.

grounding.quote:
Survival. Every known failure (a `falsified` result with its
counterexample), every planned assessment without a closed result and
every uncovered obligation is carried with the composite and survives every
join: combining conjunctions takes the union of known failures and of
planned assessments without a closed result, and recomputes uncovered
coverage over the combined obligations. A known failure and a gap of
either kind survive every join. Common agreement among contributors
cannot discard a constraint or a material counterexample that only one
contributor found. A missing, wrong-subject, conflicted or indeterminate
mandatory result stays unresolved under the declared rule, and aggregate
satisfied status cannot replace it (P4b, P5).

constraints.statement: Every join carries known failures with counterexamples and both gap kinds: union known failures and planned assessments lacking closed results, and recompute uncovered coverage over combined obligations. Agreement cannot discard any constraint or material counterexample found by even one contributor. Missing, wrong-subject, conflicted and indeterminate mandatory results remain unresolved; aggregate satisfied cannot replace them. Every component retains its predicate and domain outcome; satisfaction of one predicate never counts for another, and uncertain effects remain distinct from failures and undecided claims.

grounding.quote:
Where every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`
and the declared basis relations disagree, the conjunction reports
`invalid_basis`, because no coherent composite basis supports the
composite predicate (§2, Basis); any gaps stay recorded by kind. Where
every mandatory returned result is `satisfied`, the declared basis
relations agree and a gap remains, the conjunction reports
`indeterminate`, because the results it holds cannot decide the composite
predicate; that value is the conjunction's own, and the gaps stay
recorded by kind. A `falsified` result that is not mandatory stays in the
conjunction's record with its predicate and is never discarded. Where
every mandatory result is `satisfied`, the declared basis relations agree
and no gap remains, a material counterexample to a mandatory constraint
falsifies the conjunction whichever contributor found it, and without one
the conjunction's value is the one its declared rule gives over the
mandatory results.

constraints.statement: Satisfied requires every mandatory result satisfied with valid applicable evidence, agreeing declared basis relations and no gap. A material counterexample to a mandatory constraint or uncovered required obligation bars success. When a mandatory returned result is nonsatisfied, the declared rule selects a nonsatisfied value from those returned; there is no universal nonsatisfied ordering. If every mandatory returned result is satisfied but required basis relations disagree, report invalid_basis while retaining gaps. If those bases agree but a gap remains, report the conjunction's own indeterminate while retaining gap kinds. If every mandatory result is satisfied, bases agree and no gap remains, any material counterexample to a mandatory constraint falsifies the conjunction regardless of contributor; otherwise use the declared rule over mandatory results. Nonmandatory falsified results remain recorded with their predicates.

grounding.quote:
Conjunction does not transfer the semantic authority of a contributing
evaluation (P6, P4a).

Composition of results. The result of composed steps for the outer
predicate is the conjunction of the steps' results, with the outer
contract's obligations as the required coverage. That each step returned
`satisfied` supports the outer predicate only where the refinement's
premises hold ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement),
Refinement).

constraints.statement: Conjunction decides only under its declared rule and transfers no contributor's semantic authority. For composed steps, conjoin their results against the outer contract's obligations as required coverage. All steps returning satisfied supports the outer predicate only where applicable refinement premises hold.
constraints.uncertainty: The full refinement premises are outside the supplied source.

conditions: The relevant family instance premises apply.

grounding.quote:
Its instance premises are: (a) a construction
with the governing basis bound at intake under ACTIVATION §1 and the
material assumptions, together written Γ here; (b) a declared domain Ω of cases, each with the inputs,
behaviour and environment material to an obligation; (c) a checker with
declared observations and an admitted evaluation relation. They are
conditions of the situations the family governs, not commitments.

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing this section does not
(P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Γ, Ω and the checker relation are instance conditions, not foundational commitments. Preservation and end-to-end arguments use premise a; assertion directions use a,b; observation sufficiency uses b,c; provenance uses a,c; quantified assurance uses c; reuse and formal representation use a. Notation states proof obligations and does not discharge them. Added choices belong respectively to the step-law owner for adequacy/bounds, construction-design owner for composition laws, obligation owner and assessor activation for Ω/interpretation, assessment-frame owner for T/π, strategy owner for paths, admitted work authority under the Product for risk policy, realisation for dependency representation/selection, RELEASE/Product for mandatory gates, and tenant a_c design under AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS for carrier/checker/projections. Consumers apply these rules without adding decisions beyond the owner.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced commitment definitions, owner authorities and some application clauses are not supplied.

conditions: Preservation through a step or end-to-end construction is claimed.
exceptions: A missing next precondition may be acquired and justified instead of established by the preceding postcondition.

grounding.quote:
An end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's
applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the
connection from the final property to Z. The preceding postcondition
must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be
acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects
require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not
establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition
compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination
and the availability of a suitable next step (P4a, P2, P6).

constraints.statement: State boundary domains, transition relations and retained/established properties, accounting for material outcomes, effects and assumptions. Completion-only relations establish nothing about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects; those retain Results and ACTIVATION result, authority and recovery contracts. Real execution's conformance to the relation is a separate obligation. End-to-end arguments establish the initial condition, each applicable premise, every boundary's compatibility and final-property connection to Z. Concurrency, branching and external effects require their own applicable composition laws; sequential drawings and local successes do not establish them or Z. Preservation does not establish progress, termination or a suitable next step.

grounding.quote:
Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate
transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound
for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or
to remain unchanged. [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement),
Exact and approximate steps, owns the per-step law and applies this
obligation to refinement steps. A
change to the governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and the
successor rules of SPEC_METHOD §4 and RELEASE §9 (P1, P6).

constraints.statement: Exact transformations preserve declared meaning. Approximate transformations state their adequacy relation and an established complete-composition bound; local tolerances cannot be presumed additive or unchanged. Changes to governing meaning/outcome follow its owner and successor rules. Algorithmic accounts state required operation, informational accounts retained meaning/distinctions, and computational bindings realisation of work/observations. Cross-account claims identify their maps and preservation obligations; human, machine or mixed execution alone discharges none. Commuting-diagram, functor and equivalence claims need categorical demonstrations.
constraints.uncertainty: Per-step refinement law, successor rules and categorical demonstration details are external references.

conditions: Assertion implications are claimed under Γ and Ω.

grounding.quote:
These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a
necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction
requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of
passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).

constraints.statement: Retain obligation scope, conditions, exceptions and alternatives; a source identifier/digest authenticates selected text but does not prove interpretation fidelity. State whether q_t is the obligation or a narrower claim and identify which implication is supported. Q_r⇒q_t makes q_t necessary; q_t⇒Q_r makes it sufficient; a stated conjunction⇒Q_r makes that conjunction sufficient. All directions are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a necessary condition does not establish Q_r, and a count of passing tests supplies no conjunction coverage or compatibility argument.

conditions: A soundness or observed satisfaction/failure claim is made.
exceptions: A relation may admit both sound satisfied and indeterminate conclusions and need not always decide.

grounding.quote:
For every s in Ω:
  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).
  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).

An observed test pass remains an
observation while the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not
become established satisfaction of the source obligation, and a reported
failure is treated the same way. The observation binding itself needs
support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or
execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim
uses its declared distribution over outcomes under Quantified assurance
below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities (P6, P5, P1).

constraints.statement: For every s∈Ω and every admitted conclusion, (π(s),sat)∈T implies q_t(s), and (π(s),fal)∈T implies not q_t(s); a favourable selected run is insufficient for universal soundness. Identify support and unresolved directions. Restricted deterministic models retain their scope; actual checker conformance and actual observation acquisition each need support. With unestablished oracle fidelity, pass and failure remain observations rather than established source-obligation satisfaction/failure. T alone supplies no probabilities. Indeterminate remains an evidence-undecidable judgment, distinct from non-performance and unresolved work/coverage states.

conditions: A checker is claimed always to decide q_t correctly from π alone.

grounding.quote:
If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth
values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between
them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate
judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a
predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision
procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations
retain their distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was
not performed (Results) (P3, P1, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Require ∀s,s'∈Ω: π(s)=π(s') ⇒ q_t(s)=q_t(s'). If identical observations admit opposite truth values, obtain further evidence, justify a narrower scope or return indeterminate; those observations cannot support sound complete decision. In a classical set model, the condition permits a predicate on the image of π but proves neither executability nor cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations remain distinct from falsehood and non-performance.

grounding.quote:
Assurance accounts for
shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,
copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,
model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.
Porting retains authorship and common dependencies (EVALUATION §3 and the
Cross-Synthesis rule of the Product that owns this corpus). Repeating
evidence does not create a new independent observation.

constraints.statement: Both assertion and execution provenance are required for their claims; execution records alone do not derive expected answers from requirements, and assessment authentication establishes neither provenance. Implementation-derived checks can support regression or a stated local property but repeating implementation decisions gives no independent upstream fidelity justification. Easier inspection/execution of a shorter assertion path is a supported design claim, not guaranteed correctness, coverage or independence. Valid implementations may differ within an acceptable relation, so output equality is not universally an oracle. Agreement permits shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis and does not identify the faulty party. Account for all material shared failure causes; different actors, model families or codebases do not establish independence. Porting retains authorship/common dependencies, and repeated evidence is no new independent observation.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed authentication and Cross-Synthesis obligations are not supplied.

conditions: Governing expectations or a shared model are being validated or corrected.

grounding.quote:
Agreement with
an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired
real-world outcome; validation of the governing expectations uses its
declared purpose and external observations through their owners, and
proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable
change authority ([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#4-change-management))
(P4a, P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Agreement with an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired real-world outcome. Validate governing expectations using declared purpose and external observations through their owners; proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow applicable change authority.

grounding.quote:
Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required
assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That
selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and
uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional
evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and
dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks
substitutes for that account (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: The actor exercising admitted work authority selects assurance for stated risk, obligations and resources, identifying material failure consequences, coverage, uncertainty and conditions for action/acceptance. Additional evidence strengthens claims only through an applicability and dependence account; test count or preference for more checks cannot substitute. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be waived by cheaper assurance.

conditions: A posterior or joint miss probability is claimed under a declared model.
exceptions: Zero-probability conditioning prefixes must be handled without inventing conditional values.

grounding.quote:
P(V | E, Γ) =
  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)
  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].

P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)
  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).

constraints.statement: Use P(V|E,Γ)=P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ)/[P(E|V,Γ)P(V|Γ)+P(E|not V,Γ)P(not V|Γ)] only with nonzero denominator; E may include agreement, disagreement or other observations, and likelihoods under faulty and nonfaulty conditions both matter. The formula supplies no missing priors/likelihoods; posterior strength is bounded by model/evidence. For M_i meaning check i misses V under specified conditions, the joint miss probability equals the product of P(M_i|V,Γ,M_1,...,M_(i−1)) with defined conditioning events. Replacing these factors by P(M_i|V,Γ) requires conditional independence. One minus joint miss is at least one detection under those conditions, not whole-product correctness. Agreement need not increase confidence when shared causes or new information change the model.

grounding.quote:
Calibration from sampled cases or injected defects supports only its
justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric
confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits
remain usable within the governing policy. No universal probability
threshold is imposed and no probability estimate is required for every
test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be
waived by a cheaper assurance plan (P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Sampled-case or injected-defect calibration supports only a justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numerical confidence remains unresolved. Qualitative evidence and stated limits remain usable within governing policy; the member imposes neither a universal threshold nor a probability estimate for every test.

conditions: Checks are selected or excluded following change Δ.

grounding.quote:
Excluding a check requires
supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change
cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not
evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves
the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create
assessment work even when no existing check covers them. A mandatory
gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of
selection ([RELEASE §8](RELEASE.md#8-acceptance)), remains applicable
(P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Keep justification and evidence-validity dependencies distinct; requirements-to-test links alone are incomplete impact models. Exclusion requires supported coverage of material dependencies and a reason Δ cannot invalidate the reused claim; absent edges prove no non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations/cases create work even without existing checks. Reassessment includes selected checks, new-obligation assessment and applicable mandatory gates, which selection cannot remove. Selection alone creates no execution evidence, and failed/indeterminate results keep their standing.

conditions: Evidence is retained for a new subject and basis.

grounding.quote:
Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new
subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and
observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are
unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The
original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability
relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither
invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent
test of the correction: the corrected subject carries its own evidence.
Known failures, unresolved coverage and their
citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an
authorised change of obligation disposes of them (P3, P4b, P6).

constraints.statement: E_new = retain_applicable(E_old,new_subject,new_basis) union E_reassessed. Retention establishes continuing claim/scope applicability, justified assertion and observation bases, and unchanged affected dependencies or an established preservation relation. Original evidence retains its original subject and is reused through a new applicability relation. Hash change alone proves neither invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent test of the correction; the corrected subject has its own evidence. Preserve known failures, unresolved coverage and citations until supported repair, reassessment or authorised obligation change disposes of them.

conditions: Governing requirements, refinements or realisations change, or recovery/assurance optimisation is undertaken.

grounding.quote:
If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need
authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a
refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the
requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation
reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the
still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,
not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and
